title: Symmetrized Block-Product Periodic Marginals in Infinite Translation-Invariant Quantum Chains
authors: Xiao Zeng, Kaiyan Yang, Lingxia Zhang, Zizhu Wang
abstract: We study local marginals in one-dimensional translation-invariant quantum systems that may hide finite-period structure. Given an $n$-site reduced density matrix, we ask whether it can be obtained by repeating a finite $p$-site block state along the chain and averaging over the $p$ lattice translations. This defines a symmetrized block-product periodic marginal problem, which provides a route both to diagnosing hidden periodic order from local data and to upper bounding ground-state energy densities of infinite translation-invariant local Hamiltonians. We develop two complementary methods. The first is a semidefinite-programming relaxation based on block permutation symmetry and positive partial transpose constraints, which outer-approximates the convex hull of such marginals and yields certified infeasibility tests. The second is a symmetrized matrix product state ansatz, which constructs explicit block-product periodic states and gives variational upper bounds. We benchmark the framework on the Majumdar-Ghosh model, transverse-field Ising, XX, XXZ, and contextuality-related spin models. The results show that the method captures the expected finite-period structure in exactly solvable cases and gives systematically improving variational energies as the period and bond dimension increase. We also formulate a periodic-NPA relaxation for translation-invariant contextuality witnesses and recover the known quantum limits in the tested examples.
summary: The paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework to test if local quantum measurements on an infinite chain are consistent with a hidden periodic structure. It uses advanced techniques like SDP relaxations and specialized Matrix Product States to calculate upper bounds on energy densities and diagnose periodicity in models ranging from Ising to XXZ type chains.
main_problem: The study investigates local reduced density matrices ($ho[n]$) in infinite translation-invariant quantum chains to determine if they are compatible with an underlying hidden finite-period structure.
main_result: The developed framework successfully diagnoses expected periodic order in exactly solvable models (like Majumdar-Ghosh) and provides systematically improving variational upper bounds on ground-state energy densities.
method: Two complementary methods are employed: a Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxation based on block symmetry, and a Symmetrized Matrix Product State (MPS) ansatz for variational bounding.
model_or_system: The work applies to one-dimensional translation-invariant quantum systems, including the Majumdar-Ghosh model, Transverse-Field Ising, XX, and XXZ spin chains. The focus is on characterizing local properties of these infinite chains.
key_observables: Ground-state energy densities ($\Delta e$) and expectation values for contextuality witnesses ($\langle E angle_{TI}$).
important_parameters: The period ($p$) of the hidden structure, the bond dimension ($D$) used in MPS, and the size of the local measurement window ($n$).
main_assumptions: The primary challenge is that exact finite characterizations of admissible reduced states are generally unavailable; approximations rely on periodic extensions (e.g., Periodic-NPA relaxation).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the construction of symmetrized marginals for small periods ($p=3, r=2$). Figure 3 compares energy error convergence ($\Delta e$) across different models based on the period $p$.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the core problem (symmetrized block-product periodic marginals), develops two mathematical tools (SDP and MPS ansatz), benchmarks these methods on several known quantum spin models, and applies them to diagnose periodicity and bound energy/contextuality.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful theoretical tools for analyzing local measurements in complex many-body systems, bridging the gap between experimentally accessible local data and the true global ground state properties of infinite chains.

We therefore repeat the calculation with multi- ple random initializations and report the lowest energy obtained. As the bond dimension increases, this local- minimum issue is no longer observed. In all simulations, convergence is declared when the change in energy be- tween consecutive sweeps is smaller than ε = 10−7.
